suicidal-thoughts.name: Suicidal thoughts
suicidal-thoughts.line: I think about ending my life.
aliases: I don't want to be alive any more.

sources.passage: In 2024, 5.5 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 14.3 million people) had serious thoughts of suicide in the past year.
In 2024, 0.8 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 2.2 million people) attempted suicide in the past year.

suicidal-thoughts.prevalence: In 2024, 5.5 percent of U.S. adults (14.3 million people) had serious thoughts of suicide and 0.8 percent (2.2 million) attempted suicide (SAMHSA NSDUH). Suicide came up in 17.9% of Crisis Text Line conversations in 2023.

serious-mental-illness.name: Mental illness
serious-mental-illness.line: I live with a mental illness that can take over my life.

sources.passage: In 2024, 5.6 percent of adults aged 18 or older (or 14.6 million people) had SMI in the past year.
In 2023, 36 million people experienced bipolar disorder, including 3.3 million adolescents aged 10–19 years
In 2023, schizophrenia affected approximately 27 million people or 1 in 300 people worldwide

serious-mental-illness.prevalence: In 2024, 5.6 percent of U.S. adults (14.6 million people) had a serious mental illness (SAMHSA NSDUH). In 2023, 36 million people worldwide experienced bipolar disorder and about 27 million, or 1 in 300, schizophrenia (WHO).

mental-health-care.name: Therapy
mental-health-care.line: I can't get or afford help for my mental health.

sources.passage: Of the 61.5 million adults aged 18 or older in 2024 who had AMI in the past year ( Figure 57 ), slightly less than half (29.5 million people) did not receive mental health treatment in the past year ( Table A.66A ). Among these 29.5 million adults with AMI in the past year who did not receive mental health treatment, 21.0 percent (or 6.1 million people) perceived an unmet need for mental health treatment in the past year
The second most common reason for not receiving treatment was thinking treatment would cost too much (65.2 percent).
Referrals for mental health and substance use disorders assistance

mental-health-care.prevalence: Of 29.5 million U.S. adults with a mental illness who got no treatment in 2024, 21.0 percent (6.1 million people) felt they needed it; among adults with an unmet need, 65.2 percent said treatment would cost too much (SAMHSA NSDUH).

memory.name: Memory
memory.line: I forget things more than I used to.

sources.passage: Overall, 11.2% of adults aged ≥45 years reported having SCD, 50.6% of whom reported SCD-related functional limitations.

memory.prevalence: Overall, 11.2% of U.S. adults aged 45 and older reported worsening or more frequent confusion or memory loss, and 50.6% of them said it limited their daily activities (CDC, BRFSS).
